Renowned

rih-NOWND — sounds like 're-NAMED': someone renowned gets named again and again until everyone knows them. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Renowned is widely known and admired; famous for something good.

The city is renowned for its music scene, drawing visitors from around the world.

Worked Example

When the chef announces a new restaurant, reservations sell out in minutes. Food critics fly in from three continents for opening night. Her name alone is enough to fill the dining room for years.

Fame combined with admiration makes someone renowned. Unlike 'notorious,' which means famous for something bad, renowned means celebrated for excellence.

How Renowned Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

famous

famous: known by very many people

celebrated

celebrated: publicly praised and honored

Antonyms

unknown

unknown: recognized by no one

forgotten

forgotten: no longer remembered

How Strong Is It? — well-known → iconic → renowned

well-known vs. renowned

well-known vs. renowned: Well-known is weaker than renowned — a well-known name is simply recognized, while a renowned one is recognized and admired.

iconic vs. renowned

iconic vs. renowned: Iconic is stronger than renowned: a renowned guitarist is famous and admired, but an iconic one has come to symbolize the entire art form.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: again and again (Latin)

root — nown- (nom-)

root — nown- (nom-): name (Latin (via Old French renomer))

Put it together

Put it together: Old French renomer meant 'to name again and again,' from Latin nomen (name). Someone renowned is spoken of repeatedly until everyone knows the name.

Use the root in a new word: nominate

Use the root in a new word: nominate: The committee nominated her for the leadership award.

Root Check

Word Choice

Renowned is almost always followed by 'for' plus the achievement that earned the fame — 'renowned for her research,' 'renowned for its beaches.'
